title: Add a dev container so contributors can start in one click

milestone.title: Contributor onboarding
milestone.description: A new contributor can clone, run, and ship a first PR without help. See docs/DEVELOPMENT-ROADMAP.md §10.

body:
Parent: #314

## Problem

`Dockerfile` and `docker-compose.yml` exist but build the **production** image — multi-stage into `nginx:alpine` serving on port 80. Running `docker compose up` gives you a static production build, not a workspace: no hot reload, no source mounting, no tooling.

So there is currently no containerised path to *developing* on this project. New contributors install Node, hope the version matches, and debug their own machines.

## Proposal

Add `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` — the free, portable standard supported by **VS Code Dev Containers** locally and **GitHub Codespaces** in the browser.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` pinned to the Node version chosen in #324.
- [ ] `postCreateCommand` runs `npm ci`.
- [ ] Port 3000 forwarded.
- [ ] Recommended extensions preinstalled: ESLint, Prettier, Tailwind CSS IntelliSense.
- [ ] Env handling documented — the container still needs `.env.local`; use Codespaces secrets rather than baking anything in.
- [ ] **Verified in both VS Code Dev Containers and a Codespace**, not just one.
- [ ] Setup documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (#295) as an alternative to local install, not a replacement.

## Why this is worth it

A contributor with no Node installed can be running the site in a browser tab in ~2 minutes. For volunteers who may be on a locked-down lab machine, a Chromebook, or Windows without a dev setup, that's the difference between contributing and not.

Codespaces includes a free monthly allowance on personal accounts. The devcontainer spec is free regardless and works fully offline via VS Code.

## Guardrails

🚫 **Never bake credentials into the devcontainer.** No `REACT_APP_SUPABASE_*` values in `devcontainer.json` — that file is committed. Use Codespaces secrets or a local `.env.local`.

⚠️ **Do not modify the production `Dockerfile` for this.** It feeds the ghcr.io image in CI. A devcontainer is a separate, additive file.

⚠️ Keep it minimal. A devcontainer that installs half a dozen tools takes minutes to build and people stop using it.

Owning skill: `vsa-build-and-env`. Depends on #324.
